brief:
A documentary about Gaza has drawn international acclaim after winning prizes at Venice, while simultaneously sparking fierce backlash in Israel, where its directors have received death threats, The Guardian reported. The film's success at the prestigious film festival contrasts sharply with the hostile response it has triggered during Israel's contentious election campaign.

The directors have faced vitriol from Israeli quarters amid the country's febrile political moment. The documentary's reception illustrates the sharp divide over how the conflict is portrayed in public discourse.
dek: As Gaza documentary wins cinematic acclaim, its directors face vitriol in Israel amid a febrile election campaign First there was a moment of stunned silence.
title: Gaza documentary draws Venice applause and Israeli death threats
